families.reason: It reads two sales records as arrays — two totals, whether the arrays hold the same numbers, and which kind sold fewest — with no matrix operation; the remaining levers are other card values and wider counts, which are not rigor.
families.missingCapability: A context product (a quantity matrix times a price column, giving revenue) answered in the Matrix Lab's operate mode, so the student decides what the product means as well as computing it.
families.teacherReason: MathMaster's sales-record generator only asks for totals read from the arrays, so it cannot yet build the matrix-product-in-context work a built-in Honors extension needs.

families.familyTitle: Is a matrix product defined? Its size and its entries
families.reason: Every version is a 2×3 times a 3×2, always defined, computed once; the depth Honors needs — that Q · P differs from P · Q, or is not even defined — cannot be generated.
families.missingCapability: An `order` knob that asks for both P · Q and Q · P (or whether one is defined, with the Matrix Lab's askDefined), so the student shows matrix multiplication is not commutative.
families.teacherReason: MathMaster's matrix-multiplication generator computes one product in one order, so it cannot yet build the does-order-matter work a built-in Honors extension needs.

families.familyTitle: A system whose coefficient matrix has no inverse
families.reason: It already asks the deeper reading (no inverse; no solution or infinitely many; which row is a multiple of which). What remains is reasoning about a parameter, which it cannot generate.
families.missingCapability: A `parameter` knob that writes one constant or coefficient as k and asks for the value(s) of k that give no solution or infinitely many, with the answer field the Matrix Lab's solve mode would need to mark it.
families.teacherReason: MathMaster's singular-system generator uses fixed numbers, so it cannot yet build the find-the-parameter work a built-in Honors extension needs.

families.familyTitle: Solve a system of three equations with matrices
families.reason: This family makes one-solution 3×3 systems solved with technology, but matrices.singularSystem3x3 now generates the systems whose coefficient matrix has no inverse — no solution or infinitely many, decided from the constants and justified by the row that is a multiple of another — marked by the Matrix Lab's shared server grader. A recipe anchored on this family can target it; none has been written yet.
families.teacherReason: MathMaster can now generate the singular systems an Honors extension on this skill needs, but no vetted built-in Honors recipe has been written for it yet, so none is added.

families.familyTitle: The multiplicative inverse of a number
families.reason: It is the lesson's Warm-Up review: the inverse of a whole number and of a fraction, that a number times its inverse is 1, and that 0 has none. Its Honors depth is the inverse of a matrix, which this family does not generate.
families.missingCapability: A Question Family for the Matrix Lab's inverse work (judgeInverse / askInverse): find or verify A⁻¹ for a 2×2 matrix, and recognize a matrix with no inverse.
families.teacherReason: MathMaster's inverse generator only works with numbers, so it cannot yet build the inverse-matrix work a built-in Honors extension needs.

families.familyTitle: Reciprocals and a negative reciprocal
families.reason: Reciprocals and negative reciprocals is Algebra I content. A built-in Algebra II Honors extension anchored on it would teach Algebra I mathematics under an Algebra II label, so an Algebra II lesson that reviews it is given none.
families.teacherReason: Reciprocals and negative reciprocals is Algebra I content, so MathMaster does not build an Algebra II Honors extension on it.

families.familyTitle: Multiply back: a monomial times a polynomial
families.reason: It is the lesson's Warm-Up review of multiplying back: a monomial times a trinomial and a negative monomial times x + q. Larger factors are its only remaining lever, which is not rigor.
families.missingCapability: A `divisor` knob that multiplies a quotient term by a quadratic divisor (−4y(y² + y − 5), textbook 5-2 #6), the multiply-back step of dividing by a degree-2 polynomial.
families.teacherReason: MathMaster's multiply-back generator only uses linear divisors, so it cannot yet build the quadratic-divisor work a built-in Honors extension needs.

families.familyTitle: Divide a polynomial by a monomial
families.reason: Every version divides a trinomial by a two-letter monomial, one term of it the divisor itself. A term that does not divide evenly (−w² + 16w + 1000 over w, textbook 5-2 #19) gives a quotient that is not a polynomial, which this family does not write.
families.missingCapability: A `remainderTerm` knob that leaves one term over the monomial (1000/w), answered as the polynomial part plus that term's numerator, with a judgment that the quotient is not a polynomial.
families.teacherReason: MathMaster's divide-by-a-monomial generator only writes terms that divide evenly, so it cannot yet build the not-a-polynomial work a built-in Honors extension needs.

families.familyTitle: Divide monomials
families.reason: It is the lesson's Warm-Up review of the quotient of powers with every exponent left positive. The Honors depth — zero and negative exponents, and a quotient raised to a power — needs an answer that is not a polynomial, which typed answers compare only as text.
families.missingCapability: A quotient-of-monomials answer form graded by value (x³ ÷ x⁵ = x⁻² = 1/x²), so the family can ask zero and negative exponents as well.
families.teacherReason: MathMaster's monomial-division generator only writes quotients with positive exponents, so it cannot yet build the negative-exponent work a built-in Honors extension needs.

families.familyTitle: Like terms, or not — and why
families.reason: It is the lesson's Warm-Up vocabulary check — like terms, or not and why — with every term already simplified, so recognizing it never needs any algebra.
families.missingCapability: An `unsimplified` knob that writes like terms in disguise (x · x² beside 4x³, 2x · 3y beside xy), so deciding needs simplifying first.
families.teacherReason: MathMaster's like-terms generator only shows simplified terms, so it cannot yet build the like-terms-in-disguise work a built-in Honors extension needs.

families.familyTitle: Long division of a cubic by x − r (a missing term)
families.reason: Every version divides a cubic with one missing term by x − r. The Honors depth — a quartic divided by a quadratic (textbook 5-2 #6) or a divisor ax + b — is a knob this family does not have, though the Polynomial Workshop's long division already draws both.
families.missingCapability: A `divisor: quadratic | scaled` knob writing a quadratic or an ax + b divisor, answered in the Workshop's long division round by round.
families.teacherReason: MathMaster's long-division generator only divides by x − r, so it cannot yet build the quadratic-divisor work a built-in Honors extension needs.

families.familyTitle: Multiply monomials
families.reason: It is the lesson's Warm-Up review of the product of powers with whole-number exponents. The Honors depth — quotients, negative and zero exponents — needs an answer that is a quotient of monomials, which typed answers compare only as text.
families.missingCapability: A quotient-of-monomials answer form graded by value (y⁴/(81x⁴), negative and zero exponents), so the family can ask the quotient and power-of-a-power rules as well.
families.teacherReason: MathMaster's monomial generator only multiplies with whole-number exponents, so it cannot yet build the quotient and negative-exponent work a built-in Honors extension needs.

families.familyTitle: Multiply a trinomial by a binomial (area model)
families.reason: Every version is a trinomial times a binomial in one letter. The area model draws up to 16 cells, but this family never asks a product of three factors, a trinomial squared or a binomial cubed.
families.missingCapability: A `shape` knob for a trinomial times a trinomial and for (an + b)³ as two area models in turn (textbook 5-1 #58–60), answered in the Workshop's area model.
families.teacherReason: MathMaster's area-model generator multiplies one trinomial by one binomial, so it cannot yet build the larger-product work a built-in Honors extension needs.

families.familyTitle: The opposite of a polynomial, and combining like terms
families.reason: It is the lesson's Warm-Up review: the opposite of one polynomial and two pairs of like terms. Wider coefficients are its only remaining lever, which is not rigor.
families.missingCapability: A `scaled` knob that subtracts multiples, k·P − m·Q (textbook 5-1 #34), so the opposite is a distribution as well as a sign change.
families.teacherReason: MathMaster's like-terms generator only changes signs and combines pairs, so it cannot yet build the distribute-then-subtract work a built-in Honors extension needs.

families.familyTitle: Profit = revenue − cost with a quadratic cost
families.reason: It writes profit = revenue − cost, simplifies it and evaluates it once. The Honors question — how many sales make the most profit, or break even — needs the vertex or zeros of the profit, which this family does not ask.
families.missingCapability: A `question: maximize | breakEven` knob that asks for the vertex or the zeros of the profit polynomial, answered by value.
families.teacherReason: MathMaster's profit generator only evaluates the profit at one number of sales, so it cannot yet build the maximize-the-profit work a built-in Honors extension needs.

families.familyTitle: Subtract polynomials, as long division does
families.reason: It is the lesson's Warm-Up review: one two-letter difference with a missing term and one long-division subtraction whose leading terms cancel. Wider coefficients are its only remaining lever, which is not rigor.
families.missingCapability: A `lines: three` knob writing the subtraction of a quadratic divisor's product (three terms, a placeholder brought down), as dividing by a degree-2 polynomial needs.
families.teacherReason: MathMaster's subtraction generator only writes two-term long-division lines, so it cannot yet build the three-term work a built-in Honors extension needs.

families.familyTitle: Subtract polynomials (a missing term)
families.reason: Every version is two cubics in one letter, one with a missing term. The Polynomial Workshop's add & subtract mode lines up terms in several letters, but this family does not write them.
families.missingCapability: A `letters: two` knob writing both polynomials in two letters (3a²b − 2ab² + …), which the Workshop's add & subtract mode already lines up by kind of term.
families.teacherReason: MathMaster's subtraction generator uses one letter, so it cannot yet build the several-letter work a built-in Honors extension needs.

families.familyTitle: Synthetic division of a quartic by x − r (a missing term)
families.reason: Every version divides a quartic with one missing term by x − r. The Honors depth — a divisor ax + b, divided through by a first (the lesson's Example 5) — is a knob this family does not have, though the Polynomial Workshop's synthetic division already draws it.
families.missingCapability: A `leading` knob writing the divisor as ax + b (a = 2 or 3), answered in the Workshop's synthetic division with its remainder-over-ax + b box.
families.teacherReason: MathMaster's synthetic-division generator only divides by x − r, so it cannot yet build the divide-through-first work a built-in Honors extension needs.

families.familyTitle: Vertex of a quadratic function
families.reason: Algebra II vertex work (A2.4B, A2.4D) rewrites ax² + bx + c in vertex form or writes a parabola from its focus and directrix; this family only asks for the vertex point.
families.missingCapability: A `form: "completeTheSquare"` mode answered with the vertex-form equation, or a Question Family for parabolaGeometryLab (modes features, equidistance, fromGeometry, equation — the lab and its server grader exist).
families.teacherReason: MathMaster has no generator for completing the square or for parabolas from their geometry yet, so it cannot build a no-AI Algebra II Honors extension for vertex work.

families.familyTitle: System of two linear equations (algebraic: one, none or infinitely many)
families.reason: Algebra II systems (A2.3A–B) are systems of three linear equations in three variables; two-variable systems, even with no or infinitely many solutions, are Algebra I depth (A.5C).
families.missingCapability: A Question Family that generates 3×3 systems for systemsWorkspace (mode "algebraic" 3×3, "matrix3" or "spatial"). Those modes and their server graders exist, and MathMaster's Algebra II Honors 3×3 lessons already use them as hand-authored questions. (matrices.solveSystem3x3 generates 3×3 systems only for the Matrix Lab, solved with technology.)
families.teacherReason: MathMaster has no generator for three-variable systems in the Systems Workspace yet, so it cannot build a no-AI Algebra II Honors extension for systems.

families.familyTitle: System of linear equations (elimination)
families.reason: Algebra II systems (A2.3A–B) are systems of three linear equations in three variables; a two-variable elimination drill has no Algebra II Honors depth.
families.missingCapability: A Question Family that generates 3×3 systems for systemsWorkspace (mode "algebraic" 3×3, "matrix3" or "spatial"). Those modes and their server graders exist, and MathMaster's Algebra II Honors 3×3 lessons already use them as hand-authored questions. (matrices.solveSystem3x3 generates 3×3 systems only for the Matrix Lab, solved with technology.)
families.teacherReason: MathMaster has no generator for three-variable systems in the Systems Workspace yet, so it cannot build a no-AI Algebra II Honors extension for systems.

families.familyTitle: System of linear equations (substitution)
families.reason: Algebra II substitution is used on linear-quadratic systems (A2.3C–D), which no registered family generates.
families.missingCapability: A Question Family for systemsWorkspace mode "linearQuadratic" (the mode and its server grader exist), with a knob for the number of intersections (0, 1 or 2).
families.teacherReason: MathMaster has no generator for linear-quadratic systems yet, so it cannot build a no-AI Algebra II Honors extension for systems by substitution.
